title: First 10 Rituals: SDK Pocket Manual (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, repeatable pocket manual for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs. Focus: the first 10 requests (developer ritual) + minimal telemetry and one-page recovery flows. Goal is to give a tiny, high-signal checklist new integrators can run in ~10 minutes and a short list of telemetry events to validate correctness and performance without heavy infra.

How to use this doc:
- Give to engineers before they write any production code.
- Run the "first-10 ritual" as a short pairing exercise with an integrator.
- Capture failures as issues with the sample tags below.

First-10 ritual (step-by-step, <10 minutes):
1) Quick creds check (1 min): set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run curl token check: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping -> expect 200 + body {"ok":true}.
2) Sanity call (1 min): run a tiny text-generation call (20 tokens): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-small","prompt":"Say hi","max_tokens":20}' -> confirm "choices" non-empty.
3) Latency spot-check (1 min): record p95 for three repeated calls at t=0, t=30s, t=60s. Note any >500ms.
4) Error surface (1 min): hit an intentionally malformed request (missing prompt) and confirm SDK surfaces a helpful error and HTTP 4xx.
5) Streaming smoke (optional, 1–2 min): run stream endpoint (if client supports) and verify partial payloads stream incrementally.
6) Token accounting check (1 min): compare billing token counts from client to console for the single sample run.
7) Telemetry emit (1 min): ensure client emitted startup event (sdk.start) and request event (sdk.request.start, sdk.request.end). Check console ingestion within 60s.
8) Fallback test (1 min): if configured with a cheap variant, induce a capacity fallback by setting policy to prefer-fallback and confirm app receives fallback indicator.
9) Rollback drill (1 min): flip feature flag that points routing to previous model and confirm responses revert.
10) Postmortem note (1 min): file a short note in the repo: /docs/integration-notes.md with "integrator: name, date, anomalies".

Minimal telemetry contract (events + required fields):
- sdk.start {"sdk_version", "env", "cfg_hash"}
- sdk.request.start {"request_id", "model", "prompt_length", "trace_id?"}
- sdk.request.end {"request_id", "status_code", "tokens_in", "tokens_out", "latency_ms"}
- sdk.error {"request_id", "error_class", "message_snippet"}
Notes: keep fields small. Trace_id optional but helpful for linking to traces. Use sample rate 1% for full token payloads; always emit counts and latency.

One-page triage (if something fails):
- Auth failure: check env var, run ping, check key rotation window in console.
- 4xx from API: capture body, copy into issue, check prompt length and reserved tokens.
- High latency: run p95 sample, check client-side batching enabled? disable and retest.
- Token mismatch: compare client-estimate vs console; suspect compression or prefix caching.
- Missing telemetry: verify SDK can reach telemetry endpoint (curl telemetry.redwood.ai/health), check network egress rules.

Sample PR description template for integrators (one paragraph):
Title: "integrate/redwood-sdk: first-10 ritual + telemetry"
Body: "This PR wires the Redwood SDK for X service. I ran the first-10 ritual (results: 10/10 steps passed except latency p95=620ms on staging). Telemetry events added per minimal contract. Rollout plan: feature-flagged for 10% then 50%. Linked issues: #1234. Steps to validate locally included in README snippet."

Short code snippet (pseudo-curl + json) to include in README:
- Export API key
- curl sanity generation (see step 2 above)
- tail -f telemetry sink (dev) -> confirm sdk.start and request events appear

Open questions to resolve before final doc:
- Standard names for request_id across languages (UUIDv4 vs short hash).
- Default event sampling and retention in dev vs prod.
- Whether to emit partial prompt text (privacy vs utility).

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize event name list and add to telemetry contract page (Confluence).
- Jonah: add the curl snippets into the SDK quickstart README and include p95 capture helper.
- María: run the ritual with two partner teams and post findings in #devexp.

Appendix: common quick-fixes (copyable):
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
- curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-small","prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":16}'

This doc is intentionally short and opinionated — the idea is to give a shared ritual that reduces friction, forces early telemetry, and makes early rollouts safe and observable. Feedback welcome in the doc comments or #devexp."
